title: Minimize runtime footprint: coordinated SDK bumps, contract audit, and deprecation plan
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Goal: reduce per-deployment client footprint and transient dependency churn across Python, JS, and Go SDKs; remove a small set of legacy API surface fields; and provide a safe, observable rollout path. This ticket coordinates dependency upgrades (pin bumps and pruning of transitive libs), a cross-language contract audit to detect API surface changes, and a staged deprecation plan for legacy parameters that teams and customers still rely on.
tasks: Inventory transitive deps for python/js/go clients (generate SBOM-like list) - Evelyn
Classify deps by risk: security, performance, build-size, and API compatibility - Rohit
Create cross-language contract tests (fixtures + roundtrip scenarios) and add to CI - ENG-test-team
Prototype minimal compatibility-shim layer for deprecated query params (feature-flagged) - Jasmin
Open coordinated PRs: py-sdk, js-sdk, go-sdk with CHANGELOG notes and migration steps - Rohit
Run benchmark suite (latency, memory, binary size) pre/post bumps and record in dashboard - Performance Squad
Coordinate canary rollout for hosted API clients with 10% traffic for 48h - Ops
Publish migration guide and deprecation timeline in docs (Console + SDK repos) - Docs
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs (Python, JS, Go) have corresponding PRs that pass CI and include release notes
Cross-language contract tests pass with the new client versions against runtime-1.20 candidate
No customer-facing breaking changes for default configurations (warnings allowed, not errors)
Performance regressions are <2% latency and <5% memory for typical token-length distributions
Deprecation warnings are emitted server-side and client-side; migration guide published
Rollout plan executed with canary metrics tracked and rollback criterion documented
